metadata.note: Yes -- Utica had trolleys, and a lot of them. Street railway service dates back to the Utica and Westerville Railroad of 1864; the Utica Belt Line Street Railroad ran horsecars from 1886 and electrified around 1890, when, as one local history puts it, the horses were gone. On 27 November 1901 all the city and suburban streetcar lines serving Utica were unified as the Utica and Mohawk Valley Railway, which also ran a double-track INTERURBAN up the Mohawk Valley between Rome and Little Falls by way of Utica -- the line drawn here. It picked up the Rome city system in 1907 and was merged into New York State Railways in 1912, whose Utica Lines at their peak ran 17 routes with more than 100 cars. The interurban ceased in 1933; the section between Utica and Whitesboro survived until 1938; and the last streetcars of any kind on the Utica Lines ran in 1941, after which everything went to buses and the franchise was reorganised as the Utica Transit Corporation in 1948. NOTE that only the Rome - Utica - Little Falls interurban spine is drawn. The Utica city network itself -- those 17 routes -- is NOT drawn, because no route-by-route description was found; nor is the Rome city system (three routes, 6.7 miles, electrified 1903, closed 1930).
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica_and_Mohawk_Valley_Railway (the Utica and Mohawk Valley Railway was the unification of all city and suburban streetcar lines serving Utica on 27 November 1901; it operated a double-track interurban railway between Rome and Little Falls via Utica, plus city streetcar lines in Utica and Rome; Rome system acquired 1907 -- three routes making up a 6.7-mile system, Dominic Street, Floyd Avenue and the Belt Line, electrified 1903, closed 1930; merged into New York State Railways in 1912; the Utica-Whitesboro section survived until 1938; last city streetcars ran 31 May 1941)

https://www.american-rails.com/nywintstrecrs.html (the Utica Belt Line Street Railroad dated to 1886, the line originally built by the Utica & Westerville Railroad of 1864; around 1890 Utica was electrified and the horses were gone; the Utica Lines at their peak consisted of 17 transit routes operated with more than 100 cars; the line ceased operation in 1933 except Utica-Whitesboro which survived to 1938; the last streetcars on the Utica Lines ran 12 May 1941; the franchise was reorganised as the Utica Transit Corporation in 1948)

https://www.vizettes.com/kt/ne-interurbans/ny/4-uo.htm (the Utica and Mohawk Valley Railway ran from Rome to Little Falls, operating 1901-1909 before becoming part of New York State Railways; the route paralleled much of the canal)
geometry_sources: MOSTLY A WAYPOINT ROUTE, NOT A TRACE. The Utica and Mohawk Valley ran largely in the street along the Mohawk Valley, and almost none of it survives in OpenStreetMap. This line is a chain through the villages the interurban is documented to have served -- Rome, Oriskany, Whitesboro, Yorkville, Utica, Frankfort, Ilion, Mohawk, Herkimer, Little Falls -- 35.33 mi in all. The ONE genuinely traced piece is 2.99 mi of private right-of-way east of Herkimer, taken from the OSM ways named 'Utica & Mohawk Valley' and tagged abandoned:railway=tram with electrified=yes; that stretch is real alignment. Everything else is straight chords between village centres and should be read as indicative of the corridor, not of the alignment. No route mileage was found in the sources, so there is nothing to check the total against.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Frequencies and speeds are estimates. Sources conflict on when the U&MV passed to New York State Railways -- 1912 per Wikipedia, 1909 per vizettes.com -- and on the date of the last streetcar, 31 May 1941 per Wikipedia against 12 May 1941 per american-rails.com; the Wikipedia dates are used here and both conflicts are recorded. No mileage for the interurban was found. The opening date of the Rome-Little Falls interurban as such is not sourced either: 1901 is the date the constituent lines were unified as the U&MV, not necessarily the date through interurban service began. The Utica and Rome CITY networks are not drawn at all.
metadata.related: Utica's steam railroads are already on this map -- see utica_black_river_railroad.geojson, utica_chenango_susquehanna_valley_railway.geojson, nyc_adirondack_division.geojson and new_york_central.geojson.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
